questions.q: Describe how the graph of $g(x) = 2^{x-3} + 1$ is obtained from the graph of $y = 2^x$, and state the asymptote of $g$.
questions.answer: Shift right 3 units and up 1 unit. Horizontal asymptote: $y = 1$.

questions.q: The graph below passes through $(0, 1)$, $(1, 2)$, and $(2, 4)$. Write the equation of the exponential function shown.
An investment of 1000 riyals grows with continuous compounding at an annual rate of 6%: $A(t) = 1000e^{0.06t}$. Find the value after 5 years, to the nearest riyal.
Determine whether each function represents growth or decay:
2000 riyals is invested at 5% annual interest, compounded monthly, using $A = P\left(1+\frac{r}{n}\right)^{nt}$.
parts: Find the value after 3 years, to the nearest riyal.
Find the value after 3 years if compounded continuously instead ($A = Pe^{rt}$), to the nearest riyal.

questions.q: How much must be invested now at 4% annual interest compounded annually to have 10,000 riyals in 8 years? Round to the nearest riyal.
Two investments start at 500 riyals: one grows at 4% per year, the other at 7% per year. Find the value of each after 10 years, to the nearest riyal, and their difference.
Rank the following functions from slowest to fastest growth as $x \to \infty$: $y=x^{10}$, $y=2^x$, $y=1.01^x$.
questions.answer: Any exponential with base $>1$ eventually outgrows any polynomial, no matter how slowly it starts. So even though $1.01^x$ grows very slowly at first, it eventually overtakes $x^{10}$. Long-run ranking (slowest to fastest): $x^{10} < 1.01^x < 2^x$.

questions.q: The graphs of $y=2^x$ (growth) and $y=\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^x$ (decay) are shown together. Use the graph to describe the symmetry relating the two curves.
questions.answer: The two curves are mirror images of each other across the $y$-axis: $\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^x=2^{-x}$, so reflecting $y=2^x$ over the $y$-axis (replacing $x$ with $-x$) produces the decay curve.

questions.q: Explain what distinguishes $e\approx2.71828$ from other exponential bases, in terms of the slope of $y=e^x$ at $x=0$.
questions.answer: The number $e$ is the unique base for which the exponential function $y=b^x$ has a tangent line slope of EXACTLY $1$ at $x=0$ — i.e., the function's instantaneous rate of change equals its own value at every point, a property no other base shares.

questions.q: A machine depreciates in value according to $V(t)=15000(0.88)^t$ (riyals, years). Find its value after 5 years, and the year in which its value first drops below 5000 riyals (to the nearest year).
State the horizontal asymptote and range of each transformed exponential function:
Write the equation of the function obtained by taking $y=e^x$, reflecting it across the $y$-axis, then shifting it down 2 units.
questions.answer: Reflecting across the $y$-axis replaces $x$ with $-x$: $y=e^{-x}$. Shifting down 2: $y=e^{-x}-2$.

questions.q: For $f(x)=3^x$, complete a short table of values at $x=-1,0,1,2,3$ and verify each value satisfies $f(x+1)=3f(x)$.
questions.answer: $f(-1)=\frac{1}{3}$, $f(0)=1$, $f(1)=3$, $f(2)=9$, $f(3)=27$. Check: $f(0)=3f(-1)=3(1/3)=1$ ✓; $f(1)=3f(0)=3$ ✓; $f(2)=3f(1)=9$ ✓; $f(3)=3f(2)=27$ ✓ — each step multiplies by the base $3$, confirming the defining property of exponential growth.
